`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8194-fields-date-widget-format-convergence`

PM dispatch (objectui PM loop). Assignee and this claim are set by the PM on behalf of the dev seat that will do the work; that dev inherits both, verifies this is the newest `Claim:` and that it names its branch, and posts **no second claim**.

⚠️ **Deliverable #1 is redoing the enumeration, not fixing four widgets.** This card says so itself, and it is right: its population is **defined by omission** — sites that render a date *without* an options bag. A grep for `toLocaleDateString` finds the ones that spell it that way; it cannot find a site that formats a date some other unpinned way. ⇒ Enumerate every date-rendering site in `@object-ui/fields` first, then ask which pass an options bag. Report the population you actually measured and the scope you covered.

The card is also explicit that its four sites are **source-confirmed, not render-measured**. Confirm each actually renders what the card predicts before changing it.

⚠️ **This is a display-convention change, and this family has a ruling history.** #7620's identical question went to the maintainer and came back as option A (converge on `formatDate`), landing as PR #8196. ⇒ If your measurement shows these four should converge the same way, that is a straightforward follow-through of a settled convention and you may implement it. But **if any site's correct answer differs** — a different reading posture, a column vs. cell distinction, anything the #7620 ruling did not contemplate — ⛔ **stop and report** rather than choosing. A silently-picked display convention is exactly what #7620 was escalated to avoid.

⛔ Scope fence: card **#8165** is running concurrently and touches **only** `packages/fields/src/widgets/file-size-guard.ts`. ⛔ Do not touch that file.

## Delivered as PR #8215, but **held** — `needs-user-decision`. The convergence is materially larger than the ruling it follows.

PM seat, session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`. `pm:dispatched` stripped, assignee cleared.

### The enumeration was redone properly, and the card was wrong by two

Re-derived **by mechanism** over the 78 non-test source files of `packages/fields/src` before anything was edited — `toLocaleDateString` 7 · `toLocaleTimeString` 2 · `toLocaleString` 4 (all number formatting) · `Intl.DateTimeFormat` 0 · `toDateString`/`toUTCString`/`toTimeString` 0 · no date library — with controls (`useDisplayLocale` fires at 29; `toLocaleDateStringXX` returns 0).

⇒ **SIX** bare no-bag sites, not the card's four. It missed the readonly `DateTimeField` and `GridField`'s datetime branch. All six were then **render**-measured in five locales, confirming the card's prediction exactly. That is what "the population is defined by omission, redo the enumeration" was for.

⭐ And the split was drawn where the dispatch asked: the four `date` sites converged; the two `datetime` sites **deliberately not**, because their home is `formatDateTime`, whose named faces (`compact` vs the verbose default) are a **second** display-convention decision the #7620 ruling does not reach. Filed as **#8209**, graded `p3`, and fenced inside PR #8215 by a `SCOPE FENCE` pin block so that card starts from a measured position rather than prose.

### ⚠️ Why I am holding rather than landing

The dev implemented, headlined the concern, and said it is *"the one call in the card I would want a second reader on."* I agree, and I can confirm the distinction from #7620's own data:

| | #7620 (ruled) | this card |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| the former spelling | an `Intl` bag **already asking for `month:'short'`** | **no bag at all** — Intl's numeric default |
| what moved | the **year token only** — `Jul 4, 2026` → `Jul 4` | the **whole face** — `7/4/2026` → `Jul 4` |
| past years | **byte-identical**, and pinned as a must-not-change row | also change: `7/4/2024` → `Jul 4, 2024` |

⇒ **There is no must-not-change row here.** The maintainer ruled A against a change where past years provably did not move; this one moves every date in every locale in both years.

The dev's case for A extending is good and I am not dismissing it: all four sites answer the question identically (the condition my dispatch set for follow-through), option B is precisely what #7620 already refused with reasoning that transfers verbatim, and option C would leave the split alive *inside a single record's detail view*, which is the defect. **I would probably rule A myself.**

But the asymmetry decides it. Asking costs a draft PR and four one-line call sites. Not asking ships a wider visible change than was sanctioned, across every readonly date field in the product. The ruling's author should confirm the extension.

**The decision:** does ruling A extend at this magnitude (**A**, what the draft implements), want re-pricing as its own decision (**B**), or split cell-shaped from widget-shaped sites (**C**, which the dev rightly notes reintroduces the split inside one detail view)?

### ⭐ A toolchain trap worth propagating beyond this card

`cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` is a **false green** in this repo: vitest sets root to the package dir, the root projects' `packages/**` globs then match nothing, and it silently runs `apps/console`'s 22 files while reporting *"Test Files 22 passed"*. Run from the repo root or via `pnpm --filter <pkg> test`. A seat could pass a whole card on that and never know.

### On the attribution-form conflict you flagged

Right to flag rather than choose. The harness instruction supersedes the dispatch's older form, so your resolution was correct. Your observation that GitHub then appended its own footer — leaving #8215 with both — is noted, and **not re-editing it was the right call**: `update_pull_request` re-sends the draft bit, which is not worth spending on a cosmetic duplicate.

## Ruling recorded — option A (director seat, decision batch #72, 2026-09-07)

Maintainer reply, verbatim: 「7749 已加入队列，其他同意」 — this card was presented with A recommended and is covered by 「其他同意」.

**Ruling: the #7620 ruling A extends to the four readonly `date` widget faces at this magnitude.** One `date` value has one display convention, chosen by `formatDate`, regardless of which surface paints it. The fact that these four sites had *no* option bag (so the whole face moves, in both years) is a consequence of their omission, not a reason for a second convention. The escape hatch for a surface that genuinely wants the full date stays what #7620 named it: an explicit `format` style honoured by both paths — ⛔ never a second bag.

Consequences:
- PR #8215 implements exactly this and is released from its hold. `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; the queue lands it as a follow-through of a settled convention.
- The two `datetime` sites (#8209, `formatDateTime`'s `compact` vs verbose faces) remain a separate decision — this ruling does **not** reach them.
- The dev's split (four `date` sites converged, two `datetime` sites fenced and filed) was the right reading of the dispatch's stop condition. Recorded.
